verdicts.note: (not flagged verify) Aubade, c. 1953, Schott ED 10330, 'treble recorder (or flute or violin) and piano', 8'26"-8'56"; dedicated to a Dolmetsch (IMSLP: Carl; composer's site: Arnold). Recorder-first piece with violin as a printed alternative; no opus number (the Op. 77 Aubade is an orchestral work). Drop it if the catalogue wants violin-first works only.

Only the set label is imprecise: the composer's site names Op. 73 Nos. 1-3 'Trois Pièces lyriques' (Elégie, Romance, Valse triste); Tallahassee is listed as No. 4.

verdicts.title: Sonata for 2 Violins and Piano
verdicts.note: Exists: 3 movements (Poco tranquillo...; Elegy: Andante sostenuto; Finale frivolo), no opus or key, dated 1964. IMSLP lists Elkin & Co., London 1964 (plate E&Co 2696) but the composer's own site calls it a 'scribal score' with the manuscript held by the estate - so the edition is a hand-copied hire score rather than an engraved print. Duration unknown (queued 18 min is a guess, leave blank). Keep only if the owner accepts this edition status.

verdicts.title: 2 Sonnets
verdicts.note: Exists: 2 Sonnets for violin & piano, Schott Mainz 1914 (Sonnet 1 plate 29982, revised ed. London 1956; dedications Daisy Kennedy / Fritz Rothschild); in print as Schott ED 14209 'Sonnet I and II' (score and part). 'Two' is not in any source - IMSLP uses the numeral. No individual titles beyond 'Sonnet 1/2'.

verdicts.title: Tallahassee Suite, Op. 73 No. 4
verdicts.note: Exists (violin & piano suite, Schott 1911, ded. and premiered by Efrem Zimbalist at Bechstein Hall, 22 Mar 1911; in print as Schott ED 1450 'Tallahassee Suite'). Only the punctuation of the title is odd. Three movements: Bygone Memories, After Sundown, Negro Air and Dance (Air et Danse nègre). Op. 73 No. 4 per IMSLP and the composer's site.
(not flagged verify) Valse triste, Op. 73 No. 3, violin & piano, Mainz: Schott 1910 (plate 28928), ded. Paul Stoeving. Set label should be 'Trois Pièces lyriques, Op. 73' (see N3).

verdicts.title: Violin Concerto
verdicts.note: (not flagged verify) 'Concerto' alone is too bare; IMSLP and Wikipedia call it Violin Concerto (no key, no opus). Composed 1925, premiered 27 Jan 1928 Birmingham (May Harrison, Boult), one movement in connected sections, c. 22 min, Schott Mainz 1928; piano reduction with solo part by the composer in print as Schott ED 12828 (plate 31949). Scott's two double concertos (1926, 1931) are not published.

(not flagged verify) Title correct: Violin Sonata No. 1 in C major, Op. 59, 4 movements, composed 1908, premiered 24 Mar 1908 (Ethel Barns / Scott), Schott London 1910 (plate 28818), rev. 1956, in print as Schott ED 1449. Only the length differs: composer's site gives 28'48" (25' by the composer's own timing); IMSLP says 30-40 min.

gaps.title: Idyll
gaps.edition: Schott ED 1950 'Idyll for solo violin' (Edition Schott)
gaps.note: Second/third sources: Wikipedia's Cyril Scott article ('Idyll, for solo violin, 1928') and the composer's site (Schott ED 1950). Duration and level are estimates.

gaps.title: Bumble-Bees (Die Hummeln)
gaps.edition: Schott ED 1949 'Bumble-Bees (Die Hummeln)' for violin (Edition Schott)
gaps.note: Listed by Schott under solo violin and on the composer's solo-instrument page (1928, Schott ED 1949); not in Wikipedia's list and I could not open the score, so the 'unaccompanied' scoring rests on those two listings. Duration and level are estimates.

gaps.title: Sonata melodica (Violin Sonata No. 2)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano, 3 movements, composed 1950, dedicated to Francois d'Albert
gaps.edition: Elkin & Co., London 1953 (plate 2289) per the composer's site; not on IMSLP
gaps.note: Second source: Wikipedia's Cyril Scott article lists 'Violin Sonata No. 2, Sonata Melodica (1950)'. Timing 22'17" from the composer's site. Probably out of print. Scott's Sonata lirica (1937), Sonata No. 3 (1955) and No. 4 (1956) have no publisher given, so they are NOT proposed.

note: WebSearch budget ran out during this composer, so the gap check relies on IMSLP (154 pages scanned), Wikipedia, the composer's own site (cyrilscott.net violin/solo pages) and Schott's catalogue page 1 of 2. Not proposed (out of scope/unpublished): Cornish Boat Song and Little Folk-Dance (violin, cello & piano trios, Schott ED 2181/2182), The Gentle Maiden (violin or cello & piano, Schott 29646, single source), Fantaisie orientale (1938), 3 Little Waltzes/Piano Pieces Op. 67/Vesperale (violin arrangements by Lange, obscure), Lullaby Op. 57 No. 2 (Barnes/Evans arrangements). Danse nègre exists only as a piano piece (Op. 58 No. 5) - no violin arrangement found; Lotus Land (arr. Kreisler, Schott BSS 31143, Kreisler Transcripts No. 9) is already in the catalogue.
